# basal 2.8.1

[![Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Hugging%20Face-basal--2.0%20models-yellow)](https://huggingface.co/collections/Remek/basal-20-6acd1712a8e443c86cd576fc)
[![Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20Hugging%20Face-basal--omni--1.0%20models-yellow)](https://huggingface.co/collections/Remek/basal-omni-10-6acea28e8b5baed2db475c1f)
[![Website](https://img.shields.io/badge/web-basal.si5.pl-0a7d5a)](https://basal.si5.pl/)
[![basal-1.0 technical report](https://img.shields.io/badge/basal--1.0%20technical%20report-PDF-b31b1b.svg)](docs/basal-1.pdf)
[![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.23022986.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23022986)

Inference engine and models for **basal-2.0** and **basal-omni-1.0**: small, fast, calibrated *typed-decision* models
for Polish and English. The basal-omni models also take **images and audio** in a request (experimental).
**basal-omni-2.0-mini (preview)** is now available ([Models](#models)).

**What it is.** basal is inspired by *System 1* (fast, intuitive) decision models such as Jev: instead of a chatbot
that writes an answer, the model reads a **state** (a message, a document, a case file, retrieved passages, an agent
trace, a web page as JSON) and answers a **typed question** about it by returning a **probability for each allowed
answer**, in one forward pass, without generating text. The answer can never fall outside the options you gave, and
the probability says how sure the model is.

**What it is for: a dynamic classifier.** You describe the classes *in the request*, in plain language, per call,
instead of training a classifier for them: routing tickets and documents (up to 255 options), rule and policy
checks, questions about long documents, RAG decisions, scoring on ordered scales, the next step of an agent, judging
answers, and triage with a confidence threshold that sends uncertain cases to a person.

> The name comes from the *basal ganglia*, the part of the brain that selects one action among competing options.

## Contents

- [What is new in basal 2.8](#what-is-new-in-basal-28) · [Models](#models) · [Results](#results) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [API](#api)
- [Images and audio: basal-omni](#images-and-audio-basal-omni-experimental) · [MCP for agents](#mcp-basal-as-a-tool-for-agents) · [Documentation](#documentation)
- [Limitations](#limitations) · [Previous releases](#previous-releases) · [Citation](#citation) · [Contributors](#contributors) · [License](#license)

## What is new in basal 2.8

2.8.1 (15 November 2026): a fix for the `-FP8` checkpoints. The modes that cannot read their scales (`--mode eager`
and `mps`, and the default mode on many GPUs) loaded them without the scales and served wrong answers with no error;
they now refuse them before any download and name `--mode fast` or `--mode vllm`. Every other start answers as in
2.8.0. [WHATS_NEW](docs/WHATS_NEW.md#what-is-new-in-basal-281).

2.8.0 (8 November 2026): the 3.0 groundwork with answers unchanged. One calibration core, requests bounded before any
work, the long lane on by default (short requests no longer wait behind long documents), basal-run resumes an
interrupted run and stops when the server goes away, and your own calibration survives a model-card update. Fixes
from a second bug hunt; contributions from Dariusz Koryto, Rafal Wiktorowicz, Miłosz Kucharski and Marcin Brzeżański.
[WHATS_NEW](docs/WHATS_NEW.md#what-is-new-in-basal-280).

### Earlier: basal 2.5 and 2.6

Released 2 November 2026. Default answers to decision requests are byte-identical to 2.4.1; what is new is opt-in
unless a line says otherwise. All changes and the known limits: [WHATS_NEW](docs/WHATS_NEW.md).

2.5.1 (2 November 2026): `--prepared auto` now loads the start-up kernels shipped in the model repositories.

2.5.2 (3 November 2026): bug fixes; a question with an unknown `type` is now refused (HTTP 422) instead of
answered as `choice`. [WHATS_NEW](docs/WHATS_NEW.md#what-is-new-in-basal-252).

2.5.3 (4 November 2026): bug fixes; `basal-run --preset` works again, presets pick the Polish wording for short
Polish text without diacritics, and `basal-attach` works on Windows without symlink rights.
[WHATS_NEW](docs/WHATS_NEW.md#what-is-new-in-basal-253).

2.5.4 (5 November 2026): bug fixes; malformed requests are refused before the run, request text cannot forge a turn,

133	    return float("nan")

137	    dev = getattr(be, "dev", None)
138	    if dev is not None:
139	        kind = torch.device(dev).type
140	        if kind == "cuda":
141	            torch.cuda.synchronize()

150	def numbered_questions(paths, n, seed=0):
151	    """load_questions with the place of each item, for a message about it: ("file:line", item) pairs, the same items
152	    in the same order."""
153	    if isinstance(paths, (str, Path)):
154	        paths = [paths]
155	    qs = []
156	    for p in paths:
157	        for i, line in enumerate(read_lines(p), 1):
158	            if not line.strip():
159	                continue
160	            try:
161	                q = json.loads(line)
162	            except ValueError as e:
163	                raise ValueError(f"{p}:{i}: not JSON ({e})") from None
164	            if isinstance(q, (str, list)):  # a text or a list is no question: skipped, as it always was
165	                continue
166	            if not isinstance(q, dict):
167	                raise ValueError(f"{p}:{i}: a line must be a JSON object, not {type(q).__name__}")
168	            if "options" in q:
169	                qs.append((f"{p}:{i}", q))
170	    random.Random(seed).shuffle(qs)  # the permutation depends on the length only: the order of load_questions
171	    return qs[:n]

174	def load_questions(paths, n, seed=0):
175	    """Simple-format items {"state", "question", "options", "gold"?} from one or more JSONL files (full-request lines
176	    with "questions" are skipped). A line that is not JSON, or JSON that is no object, is a ValueError naming its file
177	    and line."""
178	    return [q for _, q in numbered_questions(paths, n, seed)]

182	    """load_questions (numbered_questions with located) for a command: its ValueError (file:line and what is wrong)
183	    ends the command with that message, not a traceback."""
184	    try:
185	        return (numbered_questions if located else load_questions)(paths, n)

190	def check_gold(located):
191	    """basal-bench scores against gold, so a gold that is not an option index stops it (a wrong gold reads as option 0
192	    and shows an accuracy of 0.9 or 1.0 in silence). located: numbered_questions. Only the bench calls this:
193	    loadtest and ordercheck never read gold and take such a file as they always did."""
194	    for where, q in located:
195	        opts = q.get("options")
196	        if "gold" not in q:
197	            continue
198	        if not isinstance(opts, list):
199	            raise SystemExit(f"{where}: options must be a list, not {type(opts).__name__}")
200	        g = q["gold"]
201	        if not (isinstance(g, int) and not isinstance(g, bool) and 0 <= g < len(opts)):
202	            raise SystemExit(f"{where}: gold {g!r} of {str(q.get('question', ''))[:40]!r} is not an option index "

207	    out = []
208	    for q in qs:
209	        k = len(q["options"])

211	        prompts = [render(tok, q["state"], q["question"], [q["options"][c] for c in p], fmt=fmt) for p in perms]

219	    out = []
220	    for (q, perms, _, _), probs in zip(groups, res):
221	        canon = [0.0] * len(q["options"])

223	            for k, j in enumerate(perm):
224	                canon[j] += p[k] / len(perms)

229	def cold(be):
230	    """vLLM keeps finished prompts in its prefix cache; a repeated prompt would be answered almost for free. Clear it so
231	    that every timed call computes its prompt (the second option order may still reuse the first order's prefix, as in
232	    real serving)."""
233	    if hasattr(be, "llm"):
234	        clear = getattr(be.llm, "reset_prefix_cache", None) or getattr(be.llm, "flush_cache", None)  # vLLM / SGLang

239	def fresh(be, prompts):
240	    """llama-server and Ollama keep the last prompts in a KV / prompt cache that no call of ours can clear, and answer
241	    a repeated prompt (the warm-up of the same group, the single-order call before the two-order call) almost for free.
242	    Put a new nonce in front of the prompts of a question in a timed call so that they are computed; both option orders
243	    of the question get the same nonce, so the second order still reuses the first order's prefix, as in real serving
244	    (in the throughput call every question has its own nonce, so questions share no prefix). The nonce goes after a
245	    leading BOS text, which Ollama strips before sending the prompt (it adds BOS itself). The answers of timed calls
246	    are discarded."""
247	    if getattr(be, "http", None) is None:  # not an HTTP engine: cold() clears what there is to clear
248	        return prompts
249	    nonce = f"{random.getrandbits(64):016x}\n"
250	    bos = getattr(getattr(be, "tok", None), "bos_token", None) or ""
251	    return [p[:len(bos)] + nonce + p[len(bos):] if bos and p.startswith(bos) else nonce + p for p in prompts]

254	def timed(fn, reps, be=None):
255	    lat = []
256	    for _ in range(reps):
257	        cold(be)
258	        sync(be); t = time.perf_counter()
259	        fn()
260	        sync(be); lat.append(time.perf_counter() - t)
261	    return lat

264	def measure(be, groups, lat_n):
265	    res = []
266	    for i in range(0, len(groups), 32):
267	        res += be.run_shared([(g[2], g[3]) for g in groups[i: i + 32]])
268	    dec = decisions(groups, res)
269	    one, two = [], []
270	    for g in groups[: lat_n + 5]:
271	        be.run([g[2][0]], [g[3][0]]); be.run_shared([(g[2], g[3])])  # warm-up of the shapes
272	        one += timed(lambda: be.run(fresh(be, [g[2][0]]), [g[3][0]]), 1, be)
273	        two += timed(lambda: be.run_shared([(fresh(be, g[2]), g[3])]), 1, be)
274	    one, two = sorted(one[5:]), sorted(two[5:])
275	    chunk = groups[: 16 * 8]
276	    be.run_shared([(g[2], g[3]) for g in chunk[:16]])
277	    t = sum(timed(lambda: [be.run_shared([(fresh(be, g[2]), g[3]) for g in chunk[i: i + 16]]) for i in range(0, len(chunk), 16)], 1, be))
278	    return dec, dict(lat1_ms=statistics.median(one) * 1000, lat2_ms=statistics.median(two) * 1000,
279	                     lat2_p95_ms=two[math.ceil(0.95 * len(two)) - 1] * 1000, dec_s=len(chunk) / t)

312	    ap.add_argument("--out", default=None, help="write results as JSON")

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
`basal-bench` is well-suited to optimization work: it already reports **lat1_ms / lat2_ms / lat2_p95_ms / dec_s / agree / acc / mem_gb / load_s** per mode, and writes JSON with `--out`. Crucially it has an `agree` metric against a reference mode — that's your correctness guard: an optimization that makes things faster but changes the top pick will show up as `agree < 1.0`.

"""HTTP load test of a running basal server: sequential latency and throughput with concurrent clients.

  basal-loadtest --url http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/systemone --questions basal/examples/questions.jsonl
  basal-loadtest --url http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/systemone --synthetic 1500 --concurrency 16   # ~1.5k-token states
  basal-loadtest --url http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/systemone --synthetic 1500 --determinism 100

--determinism N asks N requests one at a time, then the same N again mixed with N other requests at --concurrency, and
compares the returned probabilities exactly (a server started with --deterministic must return identical answers).
"""
import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import math
import statistics
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

from . import synth
from .bench import DEFAULT_QUESTIONS, questions_or_exit
from .cli import add_api_key, headers, refused


def body(q, early_exit=None, questions=1):
    """One request: the item's question, or (questions > 1) that many fixed questions over the item's state (SOAM)."""
    if questions > 1:
        from .identity import QUESTIONS
        from .prompt import lang_of
        qs = QUESTIONS[lang_of(q["state"])][:questions]
    else:
        qs = [(q["question"], q["options"])]
    b = {"state": q["state"], "questions": {
        f"q{i}": {"type": "choice", "instructions": t, "option_keys": "hide",
                  "criteria": {f"option_{k + 1}": o for k, o in enumerate(opts)}} for i, (t, opts) in enumerate(qs)}}
    if early_exit:
        b["early_exit"] = early_exit
    return b

# Hardware: which mode on which GPU

**What these numbers are.** The tables below were measured with the **basal-1.0 weights and engine** (offline,
`basal-bench`). basal-1.5 (4.5B) has the architecture of basal-1.0-4.5B and basal-1.5-mini that of basal-1.0-1.5B
(each pair is fine-tuned from the same Bielik base model), so the tables show what each GPU does with these model
sizes and which mode to choose; they are not measurements of the 1.5 models. The *accuracy* and *agreement* columns are
those of the basal-1.0 weights on our speed sample; for the accuracy of the 1.5 models see the
[v1.5.0 README](https://github.com/rkinas/basal/tree/v1.5.0#performance). basal-1.5-max (11B) and Apple Silicon have their own sections below.

**basal-1.5 release check** (one H100, `basal-serve --mode fast`, bf16, HTTP load test): one question 13.7 ms p50 /
23.8 ms p95, 64.4 decisions/s with 32 concurrent clients (basal-1.0 was not re-measured on that machine).
**basal-1.5-mini, release check** (same setup): one question 10.9 ms p50 / 15.9 ms p95, 155.8 decisions/s with 32 concurrent clients (basal-1.0-1.5B was not re-measured on that machine). Do not compare these HTTP numbers with the offline tables below.

One decision = **both option orders** (the default), batch size 1 unless stated. *dec/s*: two-order decisions per
second with 32 option-order passes per forward (offline) or 32 concurrent clients (HTTP). *Agreement*: share of
decisions whose top option equals the fp32 reference on the same machine (RTX 5090 and RTX 4090: the bf16 reference,
marked ²). Measured with `basal-bench` / `basal-loadtest` (H100, RTX PRO 6000 and RTX 5090 with the equivalent research
harness) on a private 500-item sample of the Polish/English test split. Requests with several questions are much
cheaper than separate requests since basal-1.5: see [SOAM.md](SOAM.md).

## Engines

Which engine runs where, and what is verified on basal-1.5 (the per-GPU tables further down are basal-1.0 engine-only
measurements):

<!-- engines -->
| engine | `basal-serve` mode | hardware | what it is for | quick start | status (basal-1.5, 4.5B) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **basal engine** (PyTorch) | `fast` (also `fast-nocompile`, `fp8`, `nvfp4`); `mps`; `eager --device mps\|cpu` | NVIDIA GPUs (sm80+); Apple Silicon with `mps` (packed requests on the Mac's GPU, no CUDA graphs) or `eager`; CPU with `mps --device cpu` (packed requests) or `eager` | the primary server: packed requests (SOAM), evidence spans, `fp8` on Hopper and Blackwell | `basal-serve --model Remek/basal-1.5-4.5B --mode fast` | **verified**: served check on one H100, 13.7 ms p50 per question over HTTP, 64.4 decisions/s with 32 clients |
| **vLLM** | `vllm` | NVIDIA GPUs | an alternative CUDA server | `basal-serve --model Remek/basal-1.5-4.5B --mode vllm` (extra `basal[vllm]`) | **verified offline** (one H100, `basal-bench`, 1,000 development decisions): agreement 0.994 with the fp32 engine, accuracy 0.928 vs 0.930, 147 decisions/s |
| **SGLang** | `sglang` | NVIDIA GPUs | an alternative CUDA server (RadixAttention prefix sharing) | `basal-serve --model Remek/basal-1.5-4.5B --mode sglang` (own environment: `sglang[srt]==0.5.21`, then basal with `--no-deps`) | **verified offline** (one H100, `basal-bench`, 1,000 development decisions): agreement 0.995 with the fp32 engine, accuracy 0.925 vs 0.930, 104.6 decisions/s; on Werdykt the same answer as the basal engine on 98.3% of items (97.0% for states over 8k tokens) |

**`basal-serve` is the decision layer in every row.** vLLM, SGLang, MLX, Ollama and llama.cpp run the weights; the typed answers (a calibrated probability for each of your options, both option orders, the state shared by several questions, `multi`, `act` and `facts`) come from `basal-serve --mode <engine>` in front of them, with the same HTTP API in every mode. A plain `ollama run` or `llama-cli` gives free text only. Evidence spans need the PyTorch engine (`fast`, `eager`); vLLM and SGLang start with a 4,096-token context (longer states are refused); raise it with `--max-len` (e.g. 32768 for long documents). Install and first request for each engine: [install and run](INSTALL.md).

## Recommendation

| GPU class | recommended mode | why |
|---|---|---|
| Data-centre (B300, B200, H100, H200) | `fast` (bf16) | limited by kernel launches at batch 1: FP8 gains ≤ 10% on H100 and is slower on B300, bf16 keeps decisions unchanged |
| Workstation / consumer (RTX PRO 6000, RTX 5090) | `fp8` | compute-bound; FP8 gives 1.3–1.4× at 97% agreement |
| RTX 4090 | `fast` (bf16); for speed `fast` with `basal-2.0-mini-FP8` or `basal-2.0-4.5B-FP8` | those checkpoints give 1.29× (mini) and 1.40× (4.5B) the decisions/s of bf16 ([measured](#rtx-4090-basal-20-in-bf16-its-fp8-checkpoints-and-fp8-mode)); `basal-2.0-max-FP8` loads on 24 GB but ran out of memory on a long prompt (not recommended there); `--mode fp8` (torchao) starts in about 18 minutes, which looked like a stall, and is slower per request |
| Desktop with unified memory (DGX Spark GB10) | `fp8` | memory-bandwidth-bound; FP8 halves latency |
| Batched high-throughput serving with vLLM | `vllm` + the `-FP8` checkpoint on Hopper / Ada, the `-NVFP4` checkpoint on Blackwell (RTX 50xx, RTX PRO 6000, B200, DGX Spark); see [QUANTIZATION](QUANTIZATION.md#basal-15-the-modelopt-checkpoints) | basal-1.0 NVFP4: 3.2× throughput on the DGX Spark, but −3 accuracy points; the basal-1.5 checkpoints' agreement and speed: FP8 agrees with the bf16 model on 0.979–0.989 of decisions; NVFP4 on 0.979 for max and 0.937 for basal-1.5 (−2.8 points); no NVFP4 for mini |
| A100 and other GPUs without FP8 (not measured) | `fast` | the bf16 path runs on any sm80+ GPU |
| RTX 3090 (Ampere, sm_86; measured by @krzysztofkaminski, [#33](https://github.com/rkinas/basal/issues/33)) | `fast` (bf16); `--batches compact` for basal-2.0-mini | basal-2.0-mini 13.4 ms per decision (one option order), 161.6 decisions/s with compact rows at 32 clients; basal-2.0 (4.5B) `fast` fits 24 GB from v2.3.1 (peak 23.1 GB); no `fp8` (torchao needs sm 8.9 or newer; 2.3.2 says so before loading) |
| Apple Silicon (M-series) | MLX port: `-MLX-8bit` (decisions as with bf16); `-MLX-fp4` for 8 GB Macs (about 1.4 accuracy points less on basal-1.5, 2.0 on max, 3.6 on mini: for mini prefer `-MLX-8bit` or GGUF); without MLX: `gguf` (a `-GGUF` file in process) or `mps` (PyTorch, evidence spans) | see [Apple Silicon](#apple-silicon) |

(about 1.15× faster, agreement ≥ 0.99). The basal-1.5 models do not ship exit heads; serve them with `fast`.

"""Identity gate of the fast path: every prefix-reuse path of the basal engine against the eager per-prompt reference.

  basal-bench --identity --model Remek/basal-1.5-4.5B                       # fp32: the paths' exactness
  basal-bench --identity --model Remek/basal-1.5-4.5B --dtype bfloat16      # as served
  basal-bench --identity --model Remek/basal-1.5-4.5B --dtype bfloat16 --quant fp8

Items are synthetic (basal.synth, no real data): single questions over ~1.5k-token states, requests with five
questions over one state, and long states (4-8k tokens); every question is rendered in both option orders. The
reference runs every prompt alone in an eager forward (no padding, no mask, no graph) and reads the option codes from
the full log-softmax. The paths, each through the engine's normal entry point (run_shared):

  plain          single prompts, one call each (plain CUDA graphs, padded to the length bucket)
  plain-batch    16 single prompts of different requests per call (cross-request batching)
  orders2        both orders of a question as one packed row (masked graph), one call each
  orders2-batch  16 questions per call
  soam           every question and order of a request over one state (one packed row), one call each
  soam-batch     8 requests per call
  long-plain     long single prompts (plain graphs up to 8192 tokens, an eager forward beyond)
  long-tree      long states, both orders (two passes over the root's KV cache)

Per path: readouts, argmax agreement with the reference, max and p99 |dp| over all option probabilities, how many of
the disagreements are near ties (top two within 0.02 in the reference) and, for the single questions, the agreement of
the decisions (both orders averaged, as served; also for the --questions items alone). Gate: agreement >= 0.999.
In bfloat16 any change of tensor shapes changes the rounding, so near ties can flip on any path, the plain one
included; fp32 shows whether a path is exact, and --reference plain compares every path with each prompt computed
alone in the same engine.

--questions FILE adds your own simple items (state / question / options) to the single questions; --against MODEL
takes the reference forwards from another model with the same tokenizer (the bf16 weights of an FP8 checkpoint), so
the agreement then measures the quantisation too.

The same check for every backend against the native engine, with question independence and bootstrap intervals, is
basal-agree (basal/agree.py), which also runs this gate: basal-agree --identity.
"""
import argparse
import json
import random

from pathlib import Path

@torch.no_grad()
def reference(be, toks, ids):
    if getattr(be, "gemma", None) is not None:
        return reference_gemma(be, toks, ids)
    h = be.model.model(input_ids=torch.tensor([toks], device=be.dev), use_cache=False).last_hidden_state[0, -1]
    lp = torch.log_softmax(be.model.lm_head(h).float(), -1)

"""Option-order check: how often the top pick changes when the options are shown in another order, and what averaging
over K orders (basal-serve --order-average K) gains and costs.

  basal-bench --order-check --model Remek/basal-omni-1.0-mini                  # bundled examples, serving default
  basal-bench --order-check --model Remek/basal-omni-1.0-mini --mode eager --questions dev.jsonl --average 2 4 6

Every question is read in its first M option orders (basal.server.option_orders: the given order, the reversed one,
then each rotation and its reverse; M = the largest of 3 and --average), all orders of a question in one call over
one state. Reported per mode:
  flip_reversed  share of questions whose top option (single order) differs between the given and the reversed order
  flip_rotated   the same for the order rotated by one (the first option moved last; with 2 options = reversed)
  flip_any       the top option differs in at least one of the M orders

How to work on basal: the development commands and checks, how a pull request adds its entry to the release notes,
and who contributed what, by pull request.

  [Release notes](#release-notes) · [Contributors, by pull request](#contributors-by-pull-request)

## Development commands

Run `make` or `make help` to list commands. The Makefile uses `.venv/bin/python` by default; override `PYTHON` to
use another prepared environment. Create it with `uv venv --python 3.12 .venv`, then install the hardware-specific
PyTorch build described in [Quick start](README.md#quick-start) before installing the app. For example:

```bash
make setup                         # editable app plus test dependencies
make setup EXTRAS=test,mlx,gguf     # Apple Silicon; install only the backends you need
make check                         # read-only pre-commit checks, no Git hook installation
make test                          # app tests; requires dependencies and applicable backend hardware
```

`setup` uses `uv pip install` in that environment and may install required dependencies. Launch and test targets
call Python directly: they never sync the environment, remove extras, or replace your selected PyTorch build.
Use `EXTRAS=test,fp8` or `EXTRAS=test,nvfp4` for the matching CUDA modes; keep vLLM in its own environment because
it brings its own PyTorch requirements. MLX requires Apple Silicon; MPS requires a supported Mac; CUDA graph and
torchao modes require compatible NVIDIA hardware. See [Serving modes](docs/SERVING.md#serving-modes) for backend limitations.

```bash
make serve                                      # automatic backend selection
make serve MODE=mlx MODEL=Remek/basal-2.0-mini-MLX-8bit
make serve MODE=fast-nocompile PORT=8001
make serve MODE=fast-exit ARGS='--early-exit 0.99'
make serve MODE=gguf GGUF='/path with spaces/model.gguf'
make serve MODE=ollama OLLAMA_MODEL=basal         # existing Ollama safetensors import
make run INPUT=basal/examples/questions.jsonl OUTPUT=answers.jsonl
make bench                                      # CLI-selected reference and serving modes
make bench ARGS='--modes eager-fp32 mps mlx --n 44'
make loadtest INPUT=basal/examples/questions.jsonl ARGS='--n-seq 20 --n-conc 100'
```

`MODE` selects one backend for `serve` or `bench`; omit it to retain the CLI's automatic defaults, as an empty `MODEL`
keeps their default model. The benchmark
also accepts its native modes such as `eager-fp32` and `fast-exit@0.99`. For multiple benchmark modes, use `ARGS`
as above; provide `GGUF` and `OLLAMA_MODEL` when the list includes those backends. GGUF still uses `MODEL` for
tokenizer/calibration, and Ollama requires a running service and a compatible import; see [hardware docs](docs/HARDWARE.md).
Required GGUF/Ollama values are checked early when selected through `MODE`; flags supplied through `ARGS` are
handled by the application. Serving or benchmarking can download and load models.

bundled simple questions). Output files are overwritten by the CLI; an `OUTPUT` that is the `INPUT` file is refused

Create a repository and wait for provisioning to become active by
default. Active means provisioning completed; later pushes or mirror
creation can still fail for other reasons.

With both a name and --project the repository is created directly.

In an interactive terminal, 'entire repo create' or 'entire repo create
<name>' opens a wizard instead. It asks for the project, name,
visibility and advanced options, starting from the given name (or the
current folder's), and shows a summary before creating anything. With
--json the prompts stay off stdout, which carries only the repository
object.

--project, --visibility and --object-format are the flag form: give any
of them and both a name and --project are required.

--visibility is set once the repository is ready, or straight after
creation with --no-wait: public grants read-only (pull) access to any
authenticated Entire user, private restricts it to explicit grantees.
New repositories are private, so omitting it (or the wizard's default)
leaves the repository private. If setting it fails, the command exits
nonzero, keeps the repository and prints the 'entire repo edit' that
finishes the job.

--wait-timeout must be positive. It bounds project resolution, creation,
and readiness polling after client setup, including creation with
--no-wait. The wizard's loading and create share that one budget; time
spent answering the wizard does not count. Use --no-wait
to return without confirming readiness.

If creation succeeds but readiness cannot be confirmed, the command exits
nonzero and preserves the repository result. Do not create again to
recover. With --json, stdout contains one repository object; progress
and recovery instructions go to stderr.

---
name: basal
description: Make typed decisions (route, triage, classify, moderate, guard, pick a tool) with a local basal server. Use when code or an agent must choose among options, answer yes/no, or rate something, and needs calibrated probabilities and an abstain-to-human rule instead of free text. Covers writing the state and questions, question types, presets, coverage / max_error, calibrating on your own data, and when to escalate.
license: Apache-2.0

# basal: typed decisions with calibrated confidence

basal does not generate text. You send one **state** (the data) and named **questions**; it answers every question in
one pass with a typed answer and calibrated probabilities. Use it where the output is a choice, not prose.

## Call it

A server is assumed running (`basal-serve --model <model> --port 8000`; see docs/SERVING.md). Then:

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/systemone -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "state": "Order 4471 arrived damaged. Customer wants money back, today.",
  "questions": {
    "intent":  {"type": "choice", "instructions": "What does the customer want?",
                "criteria": {"refund": "money back", "replace": "a new item", "info": "information only"}},
    "urgent":  {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Is this urgent?"},
    "tone":    {"type": "score", "instructions": "How angry is the customer?", "criteria": ["calm", "annoyed", "angry"]}}}'
```

Python: `Basal("http://127.0.0.1:8000").decide(state, questions)` (`from basal.client import Basal`). TypeScript:
`new Basal({url}).decide(state, questions)` (`clients/typescript`).

## Write a good state

- Put **everything the decision needs and nothing else** in the state: the message, the relevant record fields, the
  rule text. JSON objects are fine. Cut boilerplate, signatures and unrelated history.
- Do not put the question in the state, and do not tell the model how to answer. One state, many questions: the
  state is read once, so ask everything you need about it in the same request.
- Facts the model cannot know (today's date, a price list, a policy) belong in the state. Polish and English are both
  supported; the language follows the text (or `"lang": "pl" | "en"`).

## Write good questions

- `instructions` is one clear sentence about the state. Ask about one thing.
- Options (`criteria`) must be **mutually exclusive and exhaustive**. Always include an `other` option when the
  options do not cover everything. Describe each option in a few words: the model sees `key: description`.
- Yes/no questions state the positive case ("Does the customer ask for a refund?"), not a double negative.
- Prefer `choice` over many yes/no questions when exactly one thing is true; prefer `multi` when several can be.

## Question types

| type | use it for | read |
|---|---|---|
| `choice` | exactly one of 2-255 options | `choice`, `probabilities` |

def request_bodies(a, n):
    """n request bodies: synthetic items, or the simple items of --questions (a small file reused); SystemExit when
    there is none (a file of full requests only, or an empty one), which would loop for ever doubling no bodies."""
    qs = synth.items(n, a.synthetic, a.seed, long_frac=a.long_frac) if a.synthetic else questions_or_exit(a.questions, n)
    bodies = [body(q, a.early_exit, a.questions_per_request) for q in qs]
    if not bodies and n > 0:
        raise SystemExit(f"basal-loadtest: no simple items in {' '.join(map(str, a.questions))} (lines with \"state\", "
                         "\"question\" and \"options\"; full requests with \"questions\" are not used)")
    while len(bodies) < n:  # small question files are reused
        bodies += bodies
    return bodies


def nonnegative(s):
    v = int(s)
    if v < 0:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f"{s}: must be 0 or more")
    return v


async def run(a):
    if a.n_seq < 1:
        raise SystemExit("basal-loadtest: --n-seq must be at least 1")
    # warm-up, sequential and concurrent phases ask different requests (as far as the questions go), so an engine with
    # a prefix cache across requests (vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp) cannot answer a timed request from an earlier phase
    n = 10 + a.n_seq + a.n_conc
    bodies = request_bodies(a, n)
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=300, headers=headers(getattr(a, "api_key", None))) as c:
        for b in bodies[:10]:  # warm-up
            r = await c.post(a.url, json=b)
            if refused(a.url, r.status_code, getattr(a, "api_key", None)):
                raise SystemExit(f"basal-loadtest: {refused(a.url, r.status_code, a.api_key)}")
            r.raise_for_status()
        lat = []
        for b in bodies[10: 10 + a.n_seq]:
            t0 = time.perf_counter()
            r = await c.post(a.url, json=b)
            lat.append(time.perf_counter() - t0)
            r.raise_for_status()
        lat.sort()
        sem = asyncio.Semaphore(a.concurrency)

        async def one(b):
            async with sem:
                t0 = time.perf_counter()
                try:
                    r = await c.post(a.url, json=b)
                except httpx.HTTPError:  # a timeout or a refused connection is an error, it does not end the run
                    return time.perf_counter() - t0, 0
                return time.perf_counter() - t0, r.status_code

        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        res = await asyncio.gather(*[one(b) for b in bodies[10 + a.n_seq: n]])
        wall = time.perf_counter() - t0
    ok = sorted(x for x, s in res if s == 200)  # p95: the nearest rank, ceil(0.95 n)-th smallest (as basal-bench)
    out = dict(url=a.url, p50_ms=statistics.median(lat) * 1000, p95_ms=lat[math.ceil(0.95 * len(lat)) - 1] * 1000,
               concurrency=a.concurrency, decisions_per_s=len(ok) / wall, errors=len(res) - len(ok))
    if a.questions_per_request > 1:  # a request is several decisions; the rates above count requests
        out.update(questions_per_request=a.questions_per_request,
                   questions_per_s=len(ok) * a.questions_per_request / wall)
    print(json.dumps({k: round(v, 2) if isinstance(v, float) else v for k, v in out.items()}))
    if a.out:
        Path(a.out).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        Path(a.out).write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")


async def determinism(a, bodies):
    """The same requests alone and under load -> identical answers, max |dp|."""
    n = a.determinism
    probe, other = bodies[:n], bodies[n: 2 * n]

    def probs(r):
        r.raise_for_status()
        return [list(ans["probabilities"].values()) for ans in r.json()["answers"].values()]
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=300, headers=headers(getattr(a, "api_key", None))) as c:
        first = await c.post(a.url, json=probe[0])
        if refused(a.url, first.status_code, getattr(a, "api_key", None)):
            raise SystemExit(f"basal-loadtest: {refused(a.url, first.status_code, a.api_key)}")
        alone = [probs(first)] + [probs(await c.post(a.url, json=b)) for b in probe[1:]]
        sem = asyncio.Semaphore(a.concurrency)

        async def one(b):
            async with sem:
                return await c.post(a.url, json=b)
        mixed = [x for pair in zip(probe, other) for x in pair]
        res = await asyncio.gather(*[one(b) for b in mixed])
    loaded = [probs(r) for r in res[::2]]
    gap = lambda x, y: abs(x - y) if math.isfinite(x) and math.isfinite(y) else 1.0  # noqa: E731  NaN or inf (inf - inf is NaN) is the largest possible change, not a skipped comparison
    diffs = [1.0 if [len(pa) for pa in p] != [len(qa) for qa in q] else  # an answer that vanished under load: the largest |dp|
             max(gap(x, y) for pa, qa in zip(p, q) for x, y in zip(pa, qa)) for p, q in zip(alone, loaded)]
    top = lambda ps: max(range(len(ps)), key=ps.__getitem__)  # noqa: E731
    flips = sum(top(pa) != top(qa) for p, q in zip(alone, loaded) for pa, qa in zip(p, q))
    out = dict(url=a.url, determinism=dict(requests=n, identical=sum(d == 0.0 for d in diffs), max_abs_diff=max(diffs),
                                           decision_flips=flips, concurrency=a.concurrency,
                                           load_errors=sum(r.status_code != 200 for r in res[1::2])))
    print(json.dumps(out))
    if a.out:
        Path(a.out).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        Path(a.out).write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--url", default="http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/systemone")
    ap.add_argument("--questions", nargs="+", default=DEFAULT_QUESTIONS, help="JSONL file(s) with simple items")
    ap.add_argument("--synthetic", type=int, default=None,
                    help="synthetic items with states of about this many tokens instead of --questions (basal.synth)")
    ap.add_argument("--long-frac", dest="long_frac", type=float, default=0.0,
                    help="--synthetic: share of long states (3k-10k tokens)")
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0,
                    help="--synthetic: the items' seed (a repeated run with another seed asks states that a server "
                         "with a prefix cache has not seen)")
    ap.add_argument("--questions-per-request", dest="questions_per_request", type=int, default=1, choices=range(1, 6),
                    help="2-5: that many fixed questions over each item's state in one request (SOAM)")
    ap.add_argument("--n-seq", dest="n_seq", type=int, default=200)
    ap.add_argument("--n-conc", dest="n_conc", type=nonnegative, default=1000)
    ap.add_argument("--concurrency", type=int, default=32)
    ap.add_argument("--early-exit", dest="early_exit", default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--determinism", type=nonnegative, default=0,
                    help="N: compare N answers given alone and under load (instead of the load test)")
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=None)
    add_api_key(ap)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if a.concurrency < 1:
        raise SystemExit("basal-loadtest: --concurrency must be at least 1")
    if a.determinism:
        n = a.determinism
        bodies = request_bodies(a, 2 * n)
        if len({json.dumps(b, sort_keys=True) for b in bodies[:2 * n]}) < 2 * n:  # probe and mixed-in requests
            print("warning: fewer than 2 x N distinct requests: the mixed pass repeats requests of the probe "
                  "(a weaker test; give more questions or --synthetic)", file=sys.stderr)
        return asyncio.run(determinism(a, bodies))
    asyncio.run(run(a))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

NVIDIA GPU, with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) in a fresh environment:

```bash
uv venv --python 3.12 --allow-existing ~/basal-env && source ~/basal-env/bin/activate
uv pip install torch==2.11.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128

```

- **`--template-prefix off` for the 4.5B model** (bf16 and `-FP8`); mini and max run with the default.
- **Install torch first, from the CUDA 12.8 index**: a plain `pip install basal` may take a torch built for a newer
  CUDA than your driver. DGX Spark and B300: the cu130 build ([docs/HARDWARE.md](docs/HARDWARE.md)).
- The first start in `--mode fast` compiles the model (several minutes); `--mode fast-nocompile` starts in seconds.

Apple Silicon, with the native arm64 Python (`--python 3.12` can take an x86_64 one under Rosetta) and no torch step:

```bash
uv python install cpython-3.12-macos-aarch64-none

```

`uname -m` prints `arm64` in a terminal that does not run under Rosetta (`x86_64` under Rosetta). An environment made

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
Two facts from this machine shape the whole design:
- `HF_HOME` and `UV_CACHE_DIR` both point at `/Volumes/Vimap H3 t7/ai/cache/…`, which **is not mounted** (only `Macintosh HD` is). Any install or model download fails until those are redirected or the drive is attached. Free space on the internal disk is **36 GB**.
- This is a **fanless M4 Air on battery**. Thermal throttling and battery power management are the dominant source of benchmark noise — far larger than most optimizations you'd measure. The harness has to defend against this (AC power required, interleaved A/B ordering, repeats + spread), or your results will be noise.

A third, subtler one: `basal-bench`'s `agree` column compares modes *within one run*, so it cannot tell you whether your optimized commit changed answers vs. the baseline commit. Cross-commit answer equality needs a separate step (serve + `basal-run` on a fixed input, then diff the probability vectors).
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

options.label: Balanced: 3 interleaved repeats (Recommended)
options.description: Each commit benchmarked 3x in A/B/A/B/A/B order, reporting median and spread per metric. Flags a difference as real only when it exceeds observed run-to-run spread. Roughly 15-40 min per full record on mini.

options.label: Quick: 1 run per commit
options.description: One pass each. Fast (~5-10 min) but on a fanless Air a 5-10% apparent difference can easily be thermal drift. Good for smoke-checking the harness, not for conclusions.

options.label: Thorough: 5 interleaved repeats
options.description: Five passes each, interleaved, plus the order-check and agree gates. Tightest confidence and catches drift, but roughly an hour or more per record.

entire repo clone — Clone an Entire repository
Clone an Entire-native repo by its `/et/<project>/<repo>` ref, a GitHub mirror by its `/gh/<owner>/<repo>` ref, or a full `entire://` clone URL.

Either ref looks up where the repo is readable — a native repo's home cluster and its ready native mirrors, or a GitHub repo's mirror clusters. On a single cluster it clones directly; on more than one, it prompts you to pick which to clone from, and without a terminal it uses the repo's primary cluster. Pass --cluster to choose either way.

--nearest times a connection to each cluster and clones from the fastest, ordering the prompt by distance and replacing the primary as the no-terminal default, when the primary was measured and lost.

The timing is local and the control plane is never told where you are. Each candidate cluster does see a connection from you, where without the flag only the one you clone from would.

A full `entire://` URL already names the cluster, so it's passed straight through to `git clone` with no lookup (and --cluster is ignored). The optional [target-dir] is passed through to `git clone` either way.

# Local benchmark harness and records repo for basal optimisation work

## Context

**Problem.** You have forked `rkinas/basal` to `bajor/basal` (origin is the Entire mirror
`entire://aws-eu-central-1.entire.io/gh/bajor/basal`) and want to optimise its inference engine, working only in
your own fork with no PRs upstream. To know whether an optimisation helped, you need to run this repository's
existing benchmarks on *this* machine against *two named commits* — a baseline from the original upstream repo and
your optimised commit — and keep an explicit, detailed, machine-readable record of every run.

**Why it is not just "run `make bench`".** Three gaps:

1. **This machine is not prepared.** There is no virtualenv, `HF_HOME` and `UV_CACHE_DIR` both point at
   `/Volumes/Vimap H3 t7/ai/cache/…` which is not currently mounted, and nothing is installed.
2. **`basal-bench`'s `agree` column compares modes inside one run**, so it cannot tell you whether your commit
   changed answers relative to the baseline commit. Cross-commit answer equality needs a separate step.
3. **A fanless M4 Air is a hostile benchmark host.** Thermal throttling and battery power management produce
   run-to-run drift larger than many real optimisations. Without repeats, interleaving and a declared noise floor,
   a record would assert improvements that are measurement noise.

**Outcome.** A prepared environment on this Mac, plus a new Entire project and repo holding a benchmark harness, an
agent skill, and one immutable directory per A/B comparison that records every metric the repository can produce and
states plainly whether the candidate commit is better, worse, unchanged, or broken.

## Decisions taken (from your answers)

| Decision | Value |
|---|---|
| Records repo location | **New** Entire project, owned by `github:bajor` |
| `basal-copy` | Delete **only** that repo from project `basal-optimisations`; leave the project |
| Models | `Remek/basal-2.0-mini` (1.5B) **and** `Remek/basal-2.0-4.5B` |
| Modes | `mps`, `eager-fp32`, `mlx` / `mlx-q8`, `gguf` — everything that runs on Apple Silicon |
| Run depth | **Thorough**: 5 interleaved repeats per side |
| Weights storage | External drive at the existing `HF_HOME`; you mount it |

## Facts measured on this machine (2026-11-18/19)

- MacBook Air, `Mac16,12`, Apple M4, 10 cores (4P + 6E), **16 GB** unified memory, macOS Darwin 25.5.0, `arm64`.
- Internal disk: **36 GiB available** (228 GiB, 83 % used). Currently on **battery** (94 %).
- `python3` is Homebrew **3.14.6**; no `.venv`; nothing installed. `uv` 0.x at `~/.local/bin/uv`.
- `entire` CLI 0.12.2, logged in as `Maciek Bajor` (`github:bajor`), jurisdiction `eu`, token in Keychain.
  `entire status` is `not set up` (capture not enabled in this repo — unrelated to this task).
- Fork confirmed: `bajor/basal`, parent `rkinas/basal`. No `upstream` remote configured; no tags fetched.
- Existing Entire projects: `basal-optimisations` (1 repo: `basal-copy`), `blinds-home-system`, `fine-tuning-models`,
  `unpolar`, `gh:mirrors:…`.

### Constraints that follow, not choices

- **`eager-fp32` is impossible for the 4.5B model on 16 GB** (≈18 GB of fp32 weights). Its reference mode is
  `mps` (bf16) — which is what `basal.bench.default_modes` already picks on Apple Silicon. `eager-fp32` *does* fit
  for `mini` (≈6 GB), so mini keeps a true fp32 correctness reference.
- **Mode lists per model** (`basal-bench --modes`, first mode is the reference):
  - mini: `eager-fp32 mps mlx mlx-q8 gguf@<file>` (5)
  - 4.5B: `mps mlx mlx-q8 gguf@<file>` (4)
- **The two `entire` network commands fail inside the Bash sandbox** with
  `tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: OSStatus -26276`. This is the sandbox's filtering proxy, not a logout
  (`entire auth status` outside the sandbox reports `logged_in: true`). Every `entire` call that talks to the
  control plane needs `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true`. The skill must say so, or it will misreport auth failures.
- **`sysctl hw.memsize`, `pmset -g therm` and `powermetrics` are blocked by the sandbox.** Thermal telemetry is
  therefore not available to the harness; `pmset -g batt` works and gives AC-vs-battery, which is the check that
  actually matters. Drift is handled by repeats and interleaving instead of by reading temperature.
- **Runtime of one thorough record is roughly 4–6 hours** (2 models × 4–5 modes × 2 sides × 5 repeats, plus
  `agree`, `order-check`, load tests and `pytest`). This is inherent to the depth you chose. The harness therefore
  also ships `quick` and `standard` profiles for iteration, with `thorough` as the default for a committed record.

## Part 1 — Prepare this machine

All of this happens in `/Users/m/repos/current/basal` and `~/basal-env`; the working tree stays clean apart from one
added git remote.

### 1.1 Preflight (fails loudly, changes nothing)

1. Confirm `/Volumes/Vimap H3 t7` is mounted and `$HF_HOME` is writable. If not, stop and say so — do not silently
   fall back to the internal disk, because the weight set does not fit there with headroom.
2. Confirm `uname -m` is `arm64` (not Rosetta).
3. Confirm `pmset -g batt` reports `AC Power`. Setup may run on battery; **benchmarks must not**.
4. Record available disk on both the internal disk and the external drive.

### 1.2 Environment

```bash
export UV_CACHE_DIR="$HF_HOME/../uv"        # the existing external-drive path
uv python install cpython-3.12-macos-aarch64-none
uv venv --python cpython-3.12-macos-aarch64-none --allow-existing ~/basal-env
uv pip install --python ~/basal-env/bin/python ".[test,mlx,gguf]"   # NOT -e
```

Python **3.12**, native arm64, per `README.md#quick-start` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`. The Homebrew 3.14 is unsuitable
(`torch>=2.11`, `transformers==5.17.0`).

**The install is deliberately non-editable.** The harness benchmarks two commits by checking each out into its own
`git worktree` and running `cd <worktree> && ~/basal-env/bin/python -m basal.bench …`. With `python -m`, `sys.path[0]`
is the current directory, so the worktree's `basal/` package shadows the copy in `site-packages`; the venv supplies
only dependencies. An **editable** install would install a meta-path finder that could win over `sys.path` and
silently benchmark the wrong code. For the same reason the harness must never call the console scripts
(`basal-bench`, `basal-serve`, …) — always `python -m basal.<module>`.

`gguf` extra builds `llama-cpp-python` from source with Metal; expect several minutes on first install.
The `media` extra (torchvision, for basal-omni images/audio) is **not** installed — no omni model is benchmarked.

### 1.3 Weights

Download into `$HF_HOME` with `hf download`:

| repo | purpose | approx |
|---|---|---|
| `Remek/basal-2.0-mini` | bf16, for `eager-fp32`, `mps`, `mlx-q8` | 3 GB |
| `Remek/basal-2.0-mini-MLX-8bit` | `--modes mlx` | 1.8 GB |
| `Remek/basal-2.0-mini-GGUF` (`Q8_0` file only) | `--modes gguf@<file>` | 1.7 GB |
| `Remek/basal-2.0-4.5B` | bf16, for `mps`, `mlx-q8` | 9 GB |
| `Remek/basal-2.0-4.5B-MLX-8bit` | `--modes mlx` | 5 GB |
| `Remek/basal-2.0-4.5B-GGUF` (`Q8_0` file only) | `--modes gguf@<file>` | 5 GB |

≈25 GB total. Download single GGUF files with `--include`, not whole repos, which carry every quantisation.

### 1.4 Upstream remote

```bash
git remote add upstream https://github.com/rkinas/basal.git
git fetch upstream --tags
```

`upstream/main` is the default baseline side. This adds a remote and fetches; it does not touch your branches, and
`origin` is left exactly as it is.

### 1.5 Baseline verification at current `HEAD` (50ce799)

In order, recording output:

1. `make check` — pinned read-only pre-commit (Ruff 0.15.16, JSON/YAML/TOML/JSONL). First run downloads hook envs.
2. `~/basal-env/bin/python -m pytest -q -n auto` — 184 test files. **Record which tests fail here**, if any: a
   pre-existing failure must not later be attributed to an optimisation.
3. Smoke benchmark, mini only, so a mistake surfaces in a minute rather than four hours:
   `python -m basal.bench --model Remek/basal-2.0-mini --modes mps --n 44 --lat-n 10 --out /tmp/smoke.json`
4. Smoke `python -m basal.bench --order-check --model Remek/basal-2.0-mini`.

Steps 1–2 are the local CI gate from the guidelines, run before any benchmarking so the harness is never built on an
unknown baseline.

## Part 2 — The records repo

### 2.1 Create it

```bash
entire project create basal-benchmarks --owner github:bajor --owner-type account --json
entire repo create records --project basal-benchmarks --json        # → /et/basal-benchmarks/records
entire repo clone /et/basal-benchmarks/records /Users/m/repos/current/basal-bench-records
```

Project names must be 3–32 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens. All three calls need
`dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` (see constraints above).

### 2.2 Delete `basal-copy`

After the new repo exists and is confirmed active:
`entire repo delete basal-copy --project basal-optimisations` — read `entire agent-help repo delete` first, and
re-confirm the exact target (`01M7R64K4VAG9CDCRJ880WWHBH`) with you immediately before running it. The
`basal-optimisations` project itself stays.

### 2.3 Layout

```text
basal-bench-records/
  README.md                   what a record is and how to read one
  AGENTS.md                   points at the shared guidelines
  environment.json            the measured machine, written by preflight and refreshed per run
  INDEX.md                    one line per record, newest first, with the verdict
  harness/
    preflight.py              mount / power / disk / memory / arm64 / dependency-drift checks
    run_record.py             orchestrator: worktrees, phases, repeats, interleaving
    verdict.py                noise floor, per-metric classification, overall verdict
    compare_answers.py        cross-commit diff of two basal-run JSONL outputs
    questions/
      bench_items.jsonl       frozen question set, copied once from basal/examples at a pinned SHA
  records/
    2026-11-19T0930Z__50ce799__a1b2c3d/
      record.md               the human-readable verdict and full metric tables
      record.json             every metric, machine-readable
      meta.json               commits, env, versions, phase timings, interleave order
      answers_diff.json       cross-commit answer equality
      raw/                    every tool's own --out JSON, unmodified, one file per side/model/mode/repeat
```

Records are **append-only**: a new comparison never edits an existing directory.

### 2.4 What each run measures

Nothing is re-implemented; each phase calls an existing basal CLI and keeps its `--out` JSON verbatim in `raw/`.

| Phase | Command (per side, per model) | Metrics captured |
|---|---|---|
| Offline bench | `python -m basal.bench --modes <list> --questions harness/questions/bench_items.jsonl --out …` | `mode`, `reference_mode`, `gpu`, `n`, `load_s`, `lat1_ms`, `lat2_ms`, `lat2_p95_ms`, `dec_s`, `mem_gb`, `forward`, `acc`, `agree` |
| Order sensitivity | `python -m basal.bench --order-check …` | `flip_reversed`, `flip_rotated`, `flip_any`, `first_share`, `acc_given/reversed/rotated`, `acc_mean<K>`, `agree_mean<K>`, `lat_mean<K>_ms`, `by_k` |
| Backend agreement | `python -m basal.agree --backends <list> --out …` | readout top-1 agreement + 95 % bootstrap CI, near ties, mean/p99/max `|dp|`, decision agreement, accuracy + paired bootstrap difference, question independence, gate |
| HTTP latency | `python -m basal.server …` then `python -m basal.loadtest --out …` | `p50_ms`, `p95_ms`, `concurrency`, `decisions_per_s`, `errors`; with `--questions-per-request 5` also `questions_per_s` |
| Determinism | `python -m basal.loadtest --determinism 100` | `requests`, `identical`, `max_abs_diff`, `decision_flips`, `load_errors` |
| **Cross-commit answers** | `python -m basal.server --deterministic …` + `python -m basal.run --concurrency 1 --output …`, both sides, same input | `identical_lines`, `decision_flips`, `max_abs_dp`, `p99_abs_dp`, per-question breakdown |
| Correctness gate | `python -m pytest -q -n auto` | passed / failed / skipped, names of failing tests |

The cross-commit answer phase is the one piece `basal-bench` cannot give you, and the reason the harness exists.
`basal-serve --deterministic` plus `basal-run --concurrency 1` removes batch-shape rounding differences, so any
remaining probability change is attributable to the code change. `compare_answers.py` is the only genuinely new
logic, and it lives in the records repo — **basal itself is never modified to be measured**.

### 2.5 Defending against thermal drift

- **5 repeats per side**, and the side that runs first alternates per repeat (rep 0: baseline then candidate;
  rep 1: candidate then baseline; …). Straight A/B/A/B would let a monotonic warm-up bias every B.
- **Noise floor per metric** = the larger of the two sides' own `(max − min) / median` across its 5 repeats.
- A metric is **BETTER** / **WORSE** only when the median change exceeds `max(noise_floor, 3 %)` in the
  direction-aware sense (lower is better for latency, higher for `dec_s`); otherwise **SAME**.
- The record prints the noise floor beside every verdict, so a claim can always be checked against the spread that
  produced it.
- `preflight.py` refuses to start a benchmark on battery power, and `meta.json` records power state, disk free and
  phase wall-clock times so a suspicious record can be re-examined.

### 2.6 Verdict rules

Correctness gates are evaluated first; any failure makes the overall verdict `BROKEN`, whatever the speed:

- a `pytest` failure the baseline does not also have;
- `basal-agree` gate below `0.99` on the candidate while the baseline passes;
- cross-commit `decision_flips > 0`, or `max_abs_dp > 0.02` (0.02 is basal's own near-tie threshold, from
  `basal/identity.py` and `basal/agree.py`);
- `acc` dropping by more than the baseline's own run-to-run `acc` spread;
- `mem_gb` up more than 10 %.

Overall verdict, one of: **BROKEN** · **REGRESSION** · **NO CHANGE** · **IMPROVEMENT** ·
**IMPROVEMENT WITH CHANGED ANSWERS** (faster, gates pass, but answers moved — explicitly separated so a speed win
bought with different answers can never be read as a free win).

### 2.7 The agent skill

`basal-bench-records/.claude/skills/basal-benchmark/SKILL.md`, following the style of the existing
`basal/skills/basal/SKILL.md` (YAML front matter with `name` and a trigger-rich `description`, then ordered steps).
It will cover:

- **When it fires** — "benchmark my optimisation", "compare against upstream", "record a benchmark run".
- **Resolving the two sides** — baseline defaults to the newest `upstream/main` commit; candidate defaults to your
  current `HEAD` or a commit you name. Both are resolved to full SHAs and written into `meta.json`; no record is
  ever written for an ambiguous ref.
- **Dependency drift** — compare the `[project] dependencies` and chosen extras between the two commits. If they
  differ, record it prominently and stop rather than comparing two differently-installed environments.
- **Running** — preflight, worktrees, phases, repeats, verdict, `record.md` + `record.json`, `INDEX.md` line,
  commit and push to the records repo.
- **Profiles** — `quick` (mini, `mps`+`mlx`, 1 repeat, ~10 min) for iteration; `standard` (both models, 3 repeats);
  `thorough` (everything, 5 repeats, **default for a committed record**, 4–6 h).
- **Operational gotchas the agent would otherwise get wrong** — `python -m basal.*` never console scripts;
  `entire` needs the sandbox disabled; AC power required; the external drive must be mounted; `eager-fp32` is not
  available for 4.5B on 16 GB.
- **Acceptance criteria**, as the guidelines require.

Because the sandbox denies writes to `/Users/m/.claude/skills`, the skill is authoritative in the records repo and
is invoked by working from that repo. If you want it available while sitting in the basal checkout, you can symlink
or copy it into `~/.claude/skills/` yourself — I will give you the one-line command rather than attempt it.

## Verification

1. **Environment** — `~/basal-env/bin/python -c "import torch, mlx.core, transformers; print(torch.__version__,
   transformers.__version__, torch.backends.mps.is_available())"` prints `True`.
2. **Baseline gate** — `make check` clean; `pytest` result recorded, with any pre-existing failure named.
3. **Harness shadowing proof** — in each worktree,
   `python -c "import basal; print(basal.__file__)"` resolves inside *that worktree*, not `site-packages`. This is
   the single most important check: if it fails, every number in every record is meaningless.
4. **End-to-end dry run** — one `quick`-profile record comparing `HEAD` with `HEAD~1`. It must produce a complete
   record directory, a `NO CHANGE` verdict with `identical_lines` equal to the item count and `decision_flips == 0`
   (a docs-only commit changes no answers), and push to the records repo.
5. **Noise-floor sanity** — one `quick` record comparing `HEAD` with **itself**. Every metric must come back
   `SAME`, and the reported noise floor is then your machine's honest measurement precision. If this run reports
   anything `BETTER` or `WORSE`, the thresholds are wrong and must be widened before any real comparison is trusted.
6. **Records repo** — `entire repo list --project basal-benchmarks` shows `records`;
   `entire repo list --project basal-optimisations` no longer shows `basal-copy`.

Step 5 is the one I would not skip: it calibrates the harness against this specific fanless machine before you draw
any conclusion from it.

### 2.5 Defending against thermal drift

- **5 repeats per side**, and the side that runs first alternates per repeat (rep 0: baseline then candidate;
  rep 1: candidate then baseline; …). Straight A/B/A/B would let a monotonic warm-up bias every B.
- **Noise floor per metric** = the larger of the two sides' own `(max − min) / median` across its 5 repeats.
- A metric is **BETTER** / **WORSE** only when the median change exceeds `max(noise_floor, 3 %)` in the
  direction-aware sense (lower is better for latency, higher for `dec_s`); otherwise **SAME**.
- The record prints the noise floor beside every verdict, so a claim can always be checked against the spread that
  produced it.
- `preflight.py` refuses to start a benchmark on battery power, and `meta.json` records power state, disk free and
  phase wall-clock times so a suspicious record can be re-examined.

### 2.6 Verdict rules

Correctness gates are evaluated first; any failure makes the overall verdict `BROKEN`, whatever the speed:

- a `pytest` failure the baseline does not also have;
- `basal-agree` gate below `0.99` on the candidate while the baseline passes;
- cross-commit `decision_flips > 0`, or `max_abs_dp > 0.02` (0.02 is basal's own near-tie threshold, from
  `basal/identity.py` and `basal/agree.py`);
- `acc` dropping by more than the baseline's own run-to-run `acc` spread;
- `mem_gb` up more than 10 %.

Overall verdict, one of: **BROKEN** · **REGRESSION** · **NO CHANGE** · **IMPROVEMENT** ·
**IMPROVEMENT WITH CHANGED ANSWERS** (faster, gates pass, but answers moved — explicitly separated so a speed win
bought with different answers can never be read as a free win).

- **Profiles** — `quick` (mini, `mps`+`mlx`, 1 repeat, ~10 min) for iteration; `standard` (both models, 3 repeats);

```text
    verdict.py                noise floor, per-metric classification, overall verdict
    compare_answers.py        cross-commit diff of two basal-run JSONL outputs
    questions/
      bench_items.jsonl       frozen question set, copied once from basal/examples at a pinned SHA
  records/
    2026-11-19T0930Z__50ce799__a1b2c3d/
      record.md               the human-readable verdict and full metric tables
      record.json             every metric, machine-readable
      meta.json               commits, env, versions, phase timings, interleave order
      answers_diff.json       cross-commit answer equality
      raw/                    every tool's own --out JSON, unmodified, one file per side/model/mode/repeat
```

Records are **append-only**: a new comparison never edits an existing directory.

### 2.4 What each run measures

Nothing is re-implemented; each phase calls an existing basal CLI and keeps its `--out` JSON verbatim in `raw/`.

| Phase | Command (per side, per model) | Metrics captured |
|---|---|---|
| Offline bench | `python -m basal.bench --modes <list> --questions harness/questions/bench_items.jsonl --out …` | `mode`, `reference_mode`, `gpu`, `n`, `load_s`, `lat1_ms`, `lat2_ms`, `lat2_p95_ms`, `dec_s`, `mem_gb`, `forward`, `acc`, `agree` |
| Order sensitivity | `python -m basal.bench --order-check …` | `flip_reversed`, `flip_rotated`, `flip_any`, `first_share`, `acc_given/reversed/rotated`, `acc_mean<K>`, `agree_mean<K>`, `lat_mean<K>_ms`, `by_k` |
| Backend agreement | `python -m basal.agree --backends <list> --out …` | readout top-1 agreement + 95 % bootstrap CI, near ties, mean/p99/max `|dp|`, decision agreement, accuracy + paired bootstrap difference, question independence, gate |
| HTTP latency | `python -m basal.server …` then `python -m basal.loadtest --out …` | `p50_ms`, `p95_ms`, `concurrency`, `decisions_per_s`, `errors`; with `--questions-per-request 5` also `questions_per_s` |
| Determinism | `python -m basal.loadtest --determinism 100` | `requests`, `identical`, `max_abs_diff`, `decision_flips`, `load_errors` |
| **Cross-commit answers** | `python -m basal.server --deterministic …` + `python -m basal.run --concurrency 1 --output …`, both sides, same input | `identical_lines`, `decision_flips`, `max_abs_dp`, `p99_abs_dp`, per-question breakdown |
| Correctness gate | `python -m pytest -q -n auto` | passed / failed / skipped, names of failing tests |

The cross-commit answer phase is the one piece `basal-bench` cannot give you, and the reason the harness exists.
`basal-serve --deterministic` plus `basal-run --concurrency 1` removes batch-shape rounding differences, so any
remaining probability change is attributable to the code change. `compare_answers.py` is the only genuinely new
logic, and it lives in the records repo — **basal itself is never modified to be measured**.

### 2.5 Defending against thermal drift

- **5 repeats per side**, and the side that runs first alternates per repeat (rep 0: baseline then candidate;
  rep 1: candidate then baseline; …). Straight A/B/A/B would let a monotonic warm-up bias every B.
- **Noise floor per metric** = the larger of the two sides' own `(max − min) / median` across its 5 repeats.
- A metric is **BETTER** / **WORSE** only when the median change exceeds `max(noise_floor, 3 %)` in the
  direction-aware sense (lower is better for latency, higher for `dec_s`); otherwise **SAME**.
- The record prints the noise floor beside every verdict, so a claim can always be checked against the spread that
  produced it.
- `preflight.py` refuses to start a benchmark on battery power, and `meta.json` records power state, disk free and
  phase wall-clock times so a suspicious record can be re-examined.

### 2.6 Verdict rules

Correctness gates are evaluated first; any failure makes the overall verdict `BROKEN`, whatever the speed:

- a `pytest` failure the baseline does not also have;
- `basal-agree` gate below `0.99` on the candidate while the baseline passes;
- cross-commit `decision_flips > 0`, or `max_abs_dp > 0.02` (0.02 is basal's own near-tie threshold, from
  `basal/identity.py` and `basal/agree.py`);
- `acc` dropping by more than the baseline's own run-to-run `acc` spread;
- `mem_gb` up more than 10 %.

Overall verdict, one of: **BROKEN** · **REGRESSION** · **NO CHANGE** · **IMPROVEMENT** ·
**IMPROVEMENT WITH CHANGED ANSWERS** (faster, gates pass, but answers moved — explicitly separated so a speed win
bought with different answers can never be read as a free win).

### 2.7 The agent skill

`basal-bench-records/.claude/skills/basal-benchmark/SKILL.md`, following the style of the existing
`basal/skills/basal/SKILL.md` (YAML front matter with `name` and a trigger-rich `description`, then ordered steps).
It will cover:

- **When it fires** — "benchmark my optimisation", "compare against upstream", "record a benchmark run".
- **Resolving the two sides** — baseline defaults to the newest `upstream/main` commit; candidate defaults to your
  current `HEAD` or a commit you name. Both are resolved to full SHAs and written into `meta.json`; no record is
  ever written for an ambiguous ref.
- **Dependency drift** — compare the `[project] dependencies` and chosen extras between the two commits. If they
  differ, record it prominently and stop rather than comparing two differently-installed environments.
- **Running** — preflight, worktrees, phases, repeats, verdict, `record.md` + `record.json`, `INDEX.md` line,
  commit and push to the records repo.
- **Profiles** — `quick` (mini, `mps`+`mlx`, 1 repeat, ~10 min) for iteration; `standard` (both models, 3 repeats);
  `thorough` (everything, 5 repeats, **default for a committed record**, 4–6 h).
- **Operational gotchas the agent would otherwise get wrong** — `python -m basal.*` never console scripts;
  `entire` needs the sandbox disabled; AC power required; the external drive must be mounted; `eager-fp32` is not
  available for 4.5B on 16 GB.
- **Acceptance criteria**, as the guidelines require.

Because the sandbox denies writes to `/Users/m/.claude/skills`, the skill is authoritative in the records repo and
is invoked by working from that repo. If you want it available while sitting in the basal checkout, you can symlink
or copy it into `~/.claude/skills/` yourself — I will give you the one-line command rather than attempt it.

## Verification

1. **Environment** — `~/basal-env/bin/python -c "import torch, mlx.core, transformers; print(torch.__version__,
   transformers.__version__, torch.backends.mps.is_available())"` prints `True`.
2. **Baseline gate** — `make check` clean; `pytest` result recorded, with any pre-existing failure named.
3. **Harness shadowing proof** — in each worktree,
   `python -c "import basal; print(basal.__file__)"` resolves inside *that worktree*, not `site-packages`. This is
   the single most important check: if it fails, every number in every record is meaningless.
4. **End-to-end dry run** — one `quick`-profile record comparing `HEAD` with `HEAD~1`. It must produce a complete
   record directory, a `NO CHANGE` verdict with `identical_lines` equal to the item count and `decision_flips == 0`
   (a docs-only commit changes no answers), and push to the records repo.
5. **Noise-floor sanity** — one `quick` record comparing `HEAD` with **itself**. Every metric must come back
   `SAME`, and the reported noise floor is then your machine's honest measurement precision. If this run reports
   anything `BETTER` or `WORSE`, the thresholds are wrong and must be widened before any real comparison is trusted.
6. **Records repo** — `entire repo list --project basal-benchmarks` shows `records`;
   `entire repo list --project basal-optimisations` no longer shows `basal-copy`.

Step 5 is the one I would not skip: it calibrates the harness against this specific fanless machine before you draw
any conclusion from it.

"""Tests for the cross-commit answer diff: its verdict is what gates every record, so it must be exactly right.

  cd harness && python -m pytest test_compare_answers.py -q
"""
import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from compare_answers import NEAR_TIE, compare


def write(path: Path, rows: list[dict]) -> Path:
    path.write_text("".join(json.dumps(r) + "\n" for r in rows), encoding="utf-8")
    return path


def item(item_id: str, x: float, y: float) -> dict:
    return {"id": item_id, "answers": {"q1": {"probabilities": {"x": x, "y": y}}}}


CONFIDENT = item("a", 0.70, 0.30)      # a clear margin: a flip here is a real change of opinion
TIED = item("b", 0.505, 0.495)         # within NEAR_TIE: rounding can flip it either way


@pytest.fixture
def diff(tmp_path):
    def run(baseline: list[dict], candidate: list[dict]) -> dict:
        return compare(write(tmp_path / "base.jsonl", baseline), write(tmp_path / "cand.jsonl", candidate))
    return run


def test_given_byte_identical_answers_when_compared_then_verdict_is_identical(diff):
    result = diff([CONFIDENT, TIED], [CONFIDENT, TIED])
    assert result["verdict"] == "IDENTICAL"
    assert result["overall"]["identical"] == 2
    assert result["overall"]["max_abs_dp"] == 0.0


def test_given_a_flip_on_a_near_tie_when_compared_then_verdict_is_equivalent(diff):
    """A top-two margin below NEAR_TIE can flip on any change of rounding, so it is not a changed decision."""
    result = diff([CONFIDENT, TIED], [CONFIDENT, item("b", 0.495, 0.505)])
    assert result["verdict"] == "EQUIVALENT"
    assert result["overall"]["flips"] == 1
    assert result["overall"]["near_tie_flips"] == 1


def test_given_a_flip_on_a_confident_item_when_compared_then_verdict_is_changed(diff):
    result = diff([CONFIDENT, TIED], [item("a", 0.20, 0.80), TIED])
    assert result["verdict"] == "CHANGED"
    assert result["overall"]["flips"] == 1
    assert result["overall"]["near_tie_flips"] == 0


def test_given_probability_drift_beyond_the_threshold_when_compared_then_verdict_is_changed(diff):
    """No flip, but the probabilities moved more than rounding explains: the calibration changed."""
    result = diff([CONFIDENT], [item("a", 0.60, 0.40)])
    assert result["overall"]["flips"] == 0
    assert result["overall"]["max_abs_dp"] > NEAR_TIE
    assert result["verdict"] == "CHANGED"


def test_given_drift_below_the_threshold_when_compared_then_verdict_is_equivalent(diff):
    result = diff([CONFIDENT], [item("a", 0.69, 0.31)])
    assert result["verdict"] == "EQUIVALENT"
    assert 0.0 < result["overall"]["max_abs_dp"] <= NEAR_TIE


def test_given_a_changed_option_count_when_compared_then_verdict_is_changed(diff):
    """An option that vanished is the largest possible difference, never a skipped comparison."""
    result = diff([CONFIDENT], [{"id": "a", "answers": {"q1": {"probabilities": {"x": 1.0}}}}])
    assert result["verdict"] == "CHANGED"
    assert result["overall"]["shape_changed"] == 1
    assert result["overall"]["max_abs_dp"] == 1.0


def test_given_a_nan_probability_when_compared_then_it_counts_as_the_largest_change(diff):
    result = diff([CONFIDENT], [{"id": "a", "answers": {"q1": {"probabilities": {"x": float("nan"), "y": 0.3}}}}])
    assert result["overall"]["max_abs_dp"] == 1.0
    assert result["verdict"] == "CHANGED"


def test_given_an_errored_line_when_compared_then_it_is_reported_not_counted_as_agreement(diff):
    result = diff([CONFIDENT], [{"id": "a", "error": "connection refused"}])
    assert result["error_count"] == 1
    assert result["overall"]["compared"] == 0


def test_given_items_missing_from_one_side_when_compared_then_they_are_named(diff):
    result = diff([CONFIDENT, TIED], [CONFIDENT])
    assert result["lines"]["compared"] == 1
    assert result["lines"]["baseline_only"] == ["b"]


def test_given_several_questions_when_compared_then_the_breakdown_locates_the_change(diff):
    base = {"id": "a", "answers": {"ok": {"probabilities": {"x": 0.7, "y": 0.3}},
                                   "bad": {"probabilities": {"x": 0.7, "y": 0.3}}}}
    cand = {"id": "a", "answers": {"ok": {"probabilities": {"x": 0.7, "y": 0.3}},

    result = diff([base], [cand])
    assert result["per_question"]["ok"]["flips"] == 0
    assert result["per_question"]["bad"]["flips"] == 1
    assert result["verdict"] == "CHANGED"

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The subtle bit in `classify()` is that the threshold is `max(noise_floor, MIN_RELATIVE_CHANGE)` — **two** independent guards. The noise floor catches a thermally noisy run (if your five repeats spanned 12%, a 9% "win" is not reportable). The 3% floor catches the opposite failure: five repeats that happen to agree closely give a noise floor near zero, which would otherwise let a 0.4% difference be declared an improvement. Either guard alone is exploitable; together they aren't.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
